subject: Request: incident postmortem & incident response plan for FintechCo auth outage
message_1_subject: FintechCo: brief outage during auth handoff — request for IR plan & postmortem
message_1_body:
Hi Irene,

We experienced a ~22-minute authentication spike between 08:05–08:27 PDT this morning where ~1.4% of login attempts returned 5xx from Redwood's token endpoint. Our SREs mitigated with a client-side retry/backoff and a temporary routing change. We need two things for our internal audit:

1) A postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis.
2) Your incident response plan and any contact escalation matrix we can include in our compliance binder (SOC 2).

Can you confirm whether this is tracked as an incident on your side and share preliminary artifacts (logs, timeline, any mitigation steps taken)? We have a quarterly compliance review next week and would like the documents before then.

Thanks,
Jordan Reed
Security Ops Lead, FintechCo
jordan.reed@fintechco.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
message_2_subject: Re: FintechCo: brief outage during auth handoff — request for IR plan & postmortem
message_2_body:
Jordan — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We've opened internal incident SEC-4821 and our security team is owning the investigation.

Short answers up front: yes, this is tracked as an incident; we're preparing a preliminary timeline and a short postmortem. We'll also attach our current incident response plan and escalation matrix. I invited our security lead (Evelyn) and CS manager (Monica) to help coordinate delivery.

Can you confirm the earliest artifact you need (prelim report vs. final)? We can share a preliminary PDF within ~3 hours and a full postmortem within 24–36 hours. Is that acceptable for your compliance review?

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
Attachment: none in this message
message_3_subject: Fwd: FintechCo outage — triage notes and logs request
message_3_body:
Irene / team — forwarding my quick triage: 

- Summary: 08:05–08:27 PDT increased 5xx rate on /v1/token (auth service) correlating with a surge in long-tail token refreshes from a single client prefix.
- Immediate mitigation: rate-limited backend worker pool + temporary routing rule to a standby instance at 08:18; error rate returned to baseline by 08:27.
- Probable cause: delayed KV-cache invalidation combined with a client-side retry pattern that amplified load.

I've pulled request logs and sampling traces — see attached stub (prelim_incident_report_fintechco_2026-03-01.pdf). I'll assemble a timeline and RCA and draft the IR plan edits to address cache invalidation and the routing fallback steps.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
message_4_subject: Prelim incident report & IR plan (draft) — FintechCo auth outage
message_4_body:
Jordan — attaching our preliminary incident report and a draft of the incident response plan edits that reference the fallback routing policy. Attachments included: prelim_incident_report_fintechco_2026-03-01.pdf and redwood_ir_plan_v3.docx (draft).

Key points in the prelim: timeline with observed metric graphs, mitigation actions taken at 08:18 and 08:21, and a short list of immediate follow-ups (runbook update for cache invalidation, add circuit-breaker thresholds for token endpoint, customer-facing SLA note).

Pending: final RCA and confirmation of any customer-side mitigations you performed. Please review and flag anything sensitive you cannot share publicly; we'll produce a redacted final postmortem if needed.

Thanks,
Evelyn
message_5_subject: Final postmortem & incident response plan — FintechCo outage (SEC-4821)
message_5_body:
Jordan — attaching the finalized postmortem (final_postmortem_fintechco_2026-03-02.pdf) and the IR plan (redwood_ir_plan_v3.docx). Summary below for your audit binder: 

TL;DR: On 2026-03-01 08:05 PDT a combination of delayed KV-cache invalidation and a client retry amplification pattern caused a transient overload of the auth token service. Measures taken: 08:18 route to standby instance; 08:21 incremental throttling on backend worker pool. Error rate normalized by 08:27.

Root cause: race in cache invalidation path on a small percentage of requests which, under certain retry behavior, could create a burst of concurrent cache misses.

Action items completed/committed:
- Runbook update to add explicit cache invalidation step and health-check gating (owner: Runtime Team; due 2026-03-10).
- Circuit-breaker thresholds added to token endpoint (owner: Serving Runtime; deployed 2026-03-02).
- Added guidance to customer SDKs about exponential backoff and jitter (owner: SDK team; planned 2026-03-12).

We've redacted internal instance IDs and full trace dumps in the attached postmortem; we can provide those under NDA if needed. If the documents meet your audit requirements, confirm and we'll mark SEC-4821 as closed.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
Attachments: final_postmortem_fintechco_2026-03-02.pdf, redwood_ir_plan_v3.docx
